justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Consultation handles video visits, Prescription coordinates e-prescriptions, AI Symptom Checker manages triage, and Consent & Policy with Context & Consent Injector enforces purpose-based patient consent.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Regional Redis Caches, SFU Media Router, and the Localization & Fallbandwidth component handle low-bandwidth optimization and caching, though background asynchronous processing patterns for heavy workflows are not detailed.
justifications.compatibility: Prescription explicitly connects to EU National e-Prescription Gateways and US Pharmacy Networks via REST and HL7 FHIR over mTLS. Identity Providers integrate via eIDAS, Login.gov, and OAuth2/OIDC as required.
justifications.usability: Patients and Licensed Clinicians are provided tailored interfaces via the Web Application & Mobile App Containers. The Offline Sync Queue and Local State & Consent Manager support users in disconnected or rural environments.
justifications.reliability: The Coturn TURN/STUN Relay, Mediasoup SFU Media Router, and Localization & Fallbandwidth component concretely ensure call continuity on connections below 300 kbit/s. Client-side Offline Sync Queue protects data integrity during disconnection.
justifications.security: Data residency is enforced using regional PostgreSQL Regional Instances, CMEK, and VPC Service Controls. Consent & Policy (OPA), WORM-compliant Medical Artifact Buckets for AI MDR audit trails, and PII-stripping egress enforce strict compliance.
justifications.maintainability: The Core Services GKE Clusters exhibit high cohesion and loose coupling with distinct microservices (Consultation, Prescription, AI Symptom Checker, Consent & Policy) isolated behind the GCP API Gateway and Istio service mesh.
justifications.portability: The architecture targets GCP europe-west3 and us-central1 effectively using containerized workloads (GKE) and standard databases. Reliance on GCP-specific services (Cloud Endpoints, KMS, Memorystore) introduces moderate cloud lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Mediasoup SFU and Coturn relays decouple heavy media traffic from Core Services, while Redis caches session state. However, dynamic regional auto-scaling of SFU media routing nodes is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: SFU capacity limits under simultaneous WebRTC room allocations
Redis session cache lookup latency during peak connection spikes
tradeoffs: Deploying centralized SFU media relays reduces client complexity but increases cloud bandwidth costs

PERF-02.justification: FastAPI microservice handles symptom checker requests efficiently at ~14 req/s. However, latency depends on third-party AI provider response times, which are subject to external network throttling and egress inspection overhead.
sensitivity_points: Third-party AI API response latency and egress filtering overhead
Pre-processor PII stripping latency before outbound dispatch
tradeoffs: Offloading inference to third parties avoids model hosting but introduces external latency dependencies

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture incorporates a Localization & Fallbandwidth component, adaptive bitrate WebRTC, Mediasoup SFU track degradation, and client-side SQLCipher storage with an Offline Sync Queue to safeguard notes.
sensitivity_points: SFU audio stream prioritization threshold when bandwidth dips below 200 kbit/s
Local client queue persistence limits during extended offline states
tradeoffs: Degrading to audio-only prioritizes call continuity over visual clinical assessment

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture designates only us-central1 for US deployment. If the entire US region fails, no secondary US region or automated regional failover within the US is configured, conflicting with residency constraints.
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary US cloud region for disaster recovery
Time required to provision infrastructure from cross-region cold backups
tradeoffs: Restricting US data to single-region deployment lowers cost but impairs cross-region disaster recovery

MOD-01.justification: The Prescription microservice isolates e-prescription logic from UI and consultation components. However, internal adapter plug-ins for country-specific formatting are bundled inside a single service rather than separate extensible adapters.
sensitivity_points: Coupling of multi-country gateway formats inside the Prescription microservice
Standardization of outbound HL7 FHIR transformation pipelines
tradeoffs: Consolidating prescription logic in one service simplifies deployment but risks regression across countries

MOD-02.justification: AI trace bundles with model version metadata are persisted to WORM storage in Medical Artifact Buckets with Object Lock, and external models are routed dynamically via Istio Egress, enabling zero-downtime rollback.
sensitivity_points: Immutability verification of AI trace bundles in WORM storage
Model version tagging consistency across external API gateways
tradeoffs: Writing immutable trace bundles to WORM storage increases storage overhead but ensures MDR compliance

SEC-01.justification: Strict isolation across europe-west3 and us-central1 via VPC Service Controls, Cloud KMS, and the Context & Consent Injector with OPA policy checks explicitly blocks cross-region access without verified patient consent.
sensitivity_points: OPA policy evaluation latency at the API Gateway context injection layer
Cryptographic isolation of regional CMEK keys
tradeoffs: Enforcing strict regional data boundaries adds authorization latency to cross-border clinician access

SEC-02.justification: Consent & Policy and the Context & Consent Injector enforce updated consent states on transactional requests. However, asynchronous propagation and deletion mechanisms for previously ingested research data in BI Ingestion are not fully specified.
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of consent revocation events to downstream BI Ingestion
Auditability of consent revocation logs in transactional storage
tradeoffs: Decoupled asynchronous consent propagation risks temporary sharing windows if synchronization delays occur
